articles.title: 15 Years Later, Jamie Lannister’s Best Game of Thrones Quote Is an All-Time Fantasy Hit
articles.summary: Many factors have helped make George R.R. Martin ’s A Song of Ice and Fire one of the most beloved fantasy series of all time, and one big reason is HBO’s adaptation of the dark fantasy epic by showrunners David Benioff and D. B. Weiss.
body: Unlike Ned Stark, whose blunt and severe demeanor left little room for elaborate remarks, Jaime Lannister seemed to have an arsenal of memorable quotes and cutting one-liners. His words reflected both his standing as Tywin Lannister’s beloved son and as Lord Commander of the Kingsguard, as well as the complicated reputation he carried throughout Westeros. To many, Jaime was a man without honor, and his sharp remarks often seemed to echo the way others judged him.
With so many banger quotes from Jaime, it’s tough to pick the best one. Still, we think we’ve narrowed it down to a line that captures a key part of Jaime’s character and a central fantasy theme.

Of all the meaningful lines Jaime delivers over Game of Thrones’ eight seasons, one perfectly highlights a key theme that often serves as a source of strength in stories, regardless of genre: love. Martin, however, twists that theme in a way that helps ensure Jaime goes down as one of fantasy’s most memorable characters.
points: Martin ’s A Song of Ice and Fire one of the most beloved fantasy series of all time, and one big reason is HBO’s adaptation of the dark fantasy epic by showrunners David Benioff and D.

articles.title: 7 Decades Later, the Most Satisfying Movie of All Time Is Free on YouTube
articles.summary: 12 Angry Men begins at the very end of a trial, just as the jury is about to go deliberate. This is a murder case where a son is being accused of stabbing his father to death. The judge reminds the jury of their duty, and that the sentence for this person, if convicted, will be death.
body: Sometimes, all I’m looking for in a movie is a really great performance. I don’t need grand adventure or killer special effects or stakes so impossibly big that I can’t relate to them. I just want to be moved by an actor (and a script) with as few frills and distractions as possible. Currently, for free (with ads) on YouTube, there is a movie that contains no less than 12 of those kinds of great performances, and it's one of the most satisfying films ever made.

The men pile in and take a few minutes to get settled, but once they do, the foreman suggests they take a vote to see where everyone stands. Of the 12-man jury, 11 of the men believe the man is guilty, while the 12th man is unsure. From there, the discussion unfolds about whether to convict or not.

This is a murder case where a son is being accused of stabbing his father to death.

articles.title: The Big Question: What's the best GTA?
articles.summary: As we teeter on the brink of gaming's biggest launch of 2026 - perhaps even decade - so many questions swirl: which GTA 6 cars will make the best vrrrrm? Is it possible for me to be any more obsessed with that Justice theme song? On a scale of one to ten, how many dongs?
body: But is it the best GTA? Vice City is certainly the GTA I've fondest memories of, even if I did mostly play it as a glorified jukebox. And as much as I've a soft spot for Chinatown Wars on Nintendo DS (a game whose propulsive style and classic top-down aesthetic did a fine job of melding GTAs old and new), Vice City is the GTA I've returned to most. But what about others on the Eurogamer team? I asked, they've answered with their own personal bests, and when they're done yammering, it's over to you - there's even a poll! And don't forget we'll be exploring the series more thoroughly as GTA Week continues.

I think, even to this day, GTA: Vice City represents what I think the best Grand Theft Auto is. The vibes, even 24 years later, are immaculate: its vision of Miami in the '80's, with all its cocaine-fueled, sun-washed Yuppie excess makes for the perfect backdrop in a game that's all about freedom and fantasy. The first half of Vice City orientates you wonderfully - casting you as Ray Liotta's arrogant, low-key psychopathic Tommy Vercetti - and letting you quietly get to know the rules of this frontier of narcotic hedonism.
points: As we teeter on the brink of gaming's biggest launch of 2026 - perhaps even decade - so many questions swirl: which GTA 6 cars will make the best vrrrrm?
Is it possible for me to be any more obsessed with that Justice theme song?
Vice City is certainly the GTA I've fondest memories of, even if I did mostly play it as a glorified jukebox.
I asked, they've answered with their own personal bests, and when they're done yammering, it's over to you - there's even a poll!

articles.title: GTA 6 Is Like The Olympics – “A Rare Cultural Moment” With Massive Ripple Effects
articles.summary: After years of development, multiple delays, and what can only be assumed to be one of the biggest production budgets ever, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19.
body: Francis Lawrence, the director of the new Hunger Games movie Sunrise on the Reaping, which comes out a day after GTA 6, has said he hopes people can find the time to play the game and watch his movie. In short, GTA 6 is seen by some as a black hole that will suck up time, attention, and money from the broader gaming economy--and even workplaces, as people dive into the 80-hour game they've been waiting a decade to play.

To help make sense of, and contextualize, the enormity of GTA 6's looming launch, GameSpot caught up with Bart Spiegel of the global professional services and research company PricewaterhouseCoopers, or PwC. He told GameSpot that GTA 6 is "something much bigger than a traditional entertainment launch," and is more akin to an event like the Olympics.
He believes GTA 6 is a "rare cultural moment" that "commands extraordinary attention and creates economic activity well beyond the event itself."
points: After years of development, multiple delays, and what can only be assumed to be one of the biggest production budgets ever, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19.

articles.title: I Can't Wait to Ignore the Main Story of GTA 6
articles.summary: It's hard to believe, but after years of waiting, we're less than a week away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. Tons of people are planning to take time off from work or school in order to sink their teeth into Rockstar's newest adventure.
body: One of the major draws of Sega's Yakuza series is that it provides a fantastic virtual tourism experience. When I visited Tokyo for the first time, I walked out of Shinjuku Station and knew exactly where I was, having spent so much time as Kiryu running around the streets of Kamurocho. I'm hoping for a similar kind of experience with GTA 6. I've never been to Miami, but I'd like to go someday. Now I can check out all those cool Art Deco buildings and take a fan boat through a swamp without spending IRL money on bottle service. Pound for pound, video games are the cheapest form of vacation out there, and this one's shaping up to be a doozy.

articles.title: Chronicles: Medieval developer declared bankruptcy on the day it announced it was in trouble, but development will continue after a $5 million reprieve from Coffee Stain
articles.summary: In late October, Chronicles: Medieval developer Raw Power Games announced that it was in trouble. Funding for its ambitious, historical sandbox strategy had suddenly been pulled, and as a result the studio was at "real risk of closing".
body: Despite this, development of Chronicles: Medieval will continue with at least some of its original creators involved, after Satisfactory developers Coffee Stain swooped in to purchase the assets and IP.

In a press release, Coffee Stain said that it submitted the winning bid in Raw Power's sale process following the company's bankruptcy, paying 36.75 million Danish Krone (around $5.42 million) for Chronicles: Medieval's intellectual property.

Rather than acquire the assets directly, however, Coffee Stain will transfer them directly to a "newly established company" that is owned 75% by Coffee Stain, and 25% by "a small group of key members of the game's original development team." Alongside paying full purchase price for Chronicles: Medieval's assets, Coffee Stain will also fund the continued development of the game.

articles.title: 25 Funniest 'Peanuts' Comics from the 1960s That Prove Charles M. Schulz Is Unbeatable
articles.summary: In 1964, Charles Schulz told a 25-part story that was some of his best work
body: The year 1964 was an election year in America. After assuming office in late November 1963 following the assassination of President John F. Kennedy, Democratic President Lyndon Johnson was running for reelection on a platform of civil rights and combating poverty. His opponent was Republican Senator Barry Goldwater, who ran on a conservative platform of smaller government. Johnson ended up winning in a landslide with 61 percent of the popular vote and 44 out of 50 states voting for him.

As is the case with every presidential election year, the race was the number one news story, and it invaded many other aspects of American life, up to and including the immensely popular comic strip Peanuts, albeit in a very Peanuts -appropriate way.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leak Seemingly Reveals Official Album's Full Track List Days Before Launch
articles.summary: The full track list for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album seems to have leaked online just days before GTA 6 's launch. Rockstar Games just can't catch a break. After weeks of unprecedented leaks were published online, even more information about GTA 6 has found its way onto the internet, this time…
body: As 13 years turns into just a few days, more leaks felt inevitable. The latest breach arrived in the form of a video shared on social media from what appears to be a Barnes & Noble-like retailer. The main clip being passed around is still up hours later and shows the front, back, and spines of the Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album's double LP vinyl. As you might have guessed, the $50 soundtrack isn't planned to hit store shelves until November 19, 2026.

Although there are likely even more tunes tucked into the game itself, an early glimpse at the GTA 6 soundtrack means we now know every song and artist featured on its official album. Rolling Stone has confirmed the track list with its sources. We won't beat around the bush; you can see the full Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album track list below.

articles.title: League of Legends: New Dawn Unveiled With Debut Trailer, Riot Announces Major Overhaul Coming in 2027
articles.summary: At the 2026 League of Legends World Championship Finals, Riot Games officially unveiled League of Legends: New Dawn. The large-scale update is scheduled for 2027 and will bring changes to the game's client, Summoner's Rift, visuals, and gameplay, marking the beginning of a new chapter for one of…
body: New Dawn introduces what Riot described as an "all-encompassing" update to League, touching almost every aspect of its experience. "This is the start of a new era for League, a new journey," said Paul Bellezza, League's executive producer, in New Dawn's first official trailer. Riot is expected to share the full reveal of New Dawn this coming January.

The announcement came with a trailer shown at Worlds Finals that offered the first glimpse of what League players can expect from New Dawn, and the changes appear to go beyond simple refreshed graphics. The first noticeable change is a redesigned champion selection screen, which looks much closer to the modern interface found in Wild Rift, League's mobile game. The footage also hints at a new or reworked rune system, which seems to have a much bigger impact on the gameplay than ever before.

articles.title: The most annoying questgivers in PC games
articles.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: Moira Brown gets a bad rap. Fallout 3's most chipper NPC, the Minnesotan menace is an inventor who sends you out on fact-finding missions to investigate the many dangers of the Wasteland. That means she puts you in harm's way quite a lot, which many players hate her for. Others just hate her voice.

I think her positive outlook makes a refreshing change of pace from, you know, everything else going on in Fallout 3. Plus she gives you an armored Vault suit just for starting her questline, and the Wasteland Survival Guide she writes with your help goes on to be a useful item in both New Vegas and Fallout 4.
What I'm saying is, there are plenty of videogame questgivers much more annoying than Moira Brown. All of the ones below, for starters. And if you disagree, you're a big meanie.

Rockstar loves to make us sit through cutscenes where our protagonist agrees to help out some of the most annoying people alive. Zero isn't alone—in GTA: San Andreas, he's got wannabe MC/janitor OG Loc for competition—but he is the winner for absolute worst.

articles.summary: Grace Ashcroft actress Angela Sant'Albano doesn't think her Resident Evil Requiem hero will "ever be a Leon character," but she's still hoping "there's a long way to go with her." The person behind one of 2026's standout video game roles laid out her hopes for the future during an interview with…
body: "I would really love to see how her relationship with Leon blossoms," Sant'Albano explained. "I think we have a beautiful mentorship, almost brotherly, sisterly relationship brewing. And I also want to know what happens with her and Emily."

Assuming you chose the 'good' ending, Resident Evil Requiem closes with the series' one-liner expert, Leon S. Kennedy, alive and Grace taking Emily under her wing. It painted a bright future for the crew, and although it almost certainly won't last, it did give the developers at Capcom plenty of room to grow new and old characters alike.

Despite some pretty deep roots in Resident Evil lore, Grace's story in the franchise is really only getting started in Resident Evil Requiem. So far, there's been no word on whether she'll stick around for additional entries and eventually stand toe-to-toe with other protagonists like Ethan Winters or Chris Redfield. Judging by the strong impression she made when her debut game launched in February, we wouldn't be surprised to see her back at some point down the line.

articles.title: 'It Felt Criminal' — Adam Driver Still Can't Believe How Disney Handled Canceled Star Wars Movie The Hunt for Ben Solo
articles.summary: Adam Driver still can't believe Disney killed his Star Wars movie, The Hunt for Ben Solo, and has now gone so far as to say that the move "felt criminal." The Kylo Ren/Ben Solo actor relived some of the darker parts of his past with the massive sci-fi franchise during a recent conversation with AP.
body: "For me it was: Steven Soderbergh wants to make a Star Wars film," Driver said. "What are we debating? It’s what it is. It’s criminal. Or it felt criminal. We’re all moving on. On to the next. And Steven already has something else that’s one of the best things he’s ever written."

We first learned about The Hunt for Ben Solo, a Skywalker Saga follow-up that explored a potential future for its title character, when Driver called it one of the "coolest scripts" he had "ever been a part of" late last year. Despite the hype, it never came to be, mostly because, according to Driver, then-Disney CEO Bob Iger and co-chairman Alan Bergman "didn't see how Ben Solo was alive."

What followed was months of additional words from those who worked on the shuttered project, including Soderbergh, who called Disney's decision to pull the plug after two-and-a-half years of work "insane." Before long, fans orchestrated their own campaign to try and save the movie, but at least as far as August 2026, Lucasfilm president Dave Filoni has said that it's not something the company is working on right now.
points: Adam Driver still can't believe Disney killed his Star Wars movie, The Hunt for Ben Solo, and has now gone so far as to say that the move "felt criminal.

articles.title: Planeswalker, Netflix's Magic: The Gathering animated series, will have a different art style for each plane
articles.summary: Netflix's Magic: The Gathering series was initially announced in 2019 with the MCU's Russo Brothers at the helm, though they left a couple of years later thanks to the all-purpose "creative differences".
body: Netflix announced soon after that actually the animated series was a go, now with Terry Matalas of Star Trek: Picard and the 12 Monkeys TV series as its head showrunner, with a teaser image showing pyromancer Chandra and leonin Ajani Goldmane silhouetted against a red sky.

Now, a mere seven years after the first reveal, there's a "sneak peek" trailer with a bunch of excited Wizards of the Coast staff, art labeled "early development", and a few seconds of Ajani and Chandra doing their stuff.

The most intriguing part is when, over a montage of 3D props including a car that looks like an art deco Batmobile from New Capenna, executive producer and supervising director Patrick Osborne says, "All the planes exist in their own pocket universe. That comes with culture, design language, architecture, and we're even making the film-making style different depending on where it is."
